_说明: 见证者点击气泡台词文件：格式=对象 {_说明, lines}，lines=字符串数组（句子池，句数不限）。
第三关元代语境：文本不绑定任何具体外貌与服饰，通用适配所有皮肤形象；性格活泼开朗、鼓励为主，融入元代‘顺木之性、大巧若拙’的大匠风范与机制引导。
抽取与播放归 Y5 波（洗牌袋整轮不重复；池空/缺文件不弹+告警）。
英文字段（2026-11-01 增补）：可选「lines_en」（与 lines 逐条等长、按句一一对应）；lines_en 缺失或缺省时回退显示中文 lines，既有中文字段一律不动。
lines: 元代的工匠最敢想敢干！木头要是长弯了，他们就顺着弯处削成大梁，这叫顺应天性！
手稳心宽，大刀阔斧！元代的卯眼往往开得肥厚开阔，别畏手畏脚的，放开胆子下刀！
若是拿不准从哪儿拼，就开一下‘锐眼’瞧瞧。这门本事你现在用得越来越顺手了嘛。
木头自己会长，人不过是帮它找个最舒服的去处。别跟它的纹理较劲，顺着来！
怎么样，现在的模样看着顺眼不？要是想换个心情，随时去衣橱里挑一身，我随叫随到～
刚才这一下卡得真结实！听听这木头咬合的闷响声，骨头缝里都透着一股扎实劲儿！
当年元代的匠人造大殿，连粗大立柱都敢直接减掉好几根，全凭榫卯大梁在头顶硬扛，厉害吧？
转一转，多换几个角度瞅瞅。正面看着严丝合缝，侧面说不定还留着退步的空当呢。
累了没？做这粗大构件确实费力气。要不歇两分钟？反正这几百年前的木头，可跑不了。
大巧若拙，大直若屈。别看它长得粗憨，内里的榫头卯眼，可比谁都精巧周密。
天赋值攒够了没？够了就去衣橱里多开几件新衣裳，我好几个模样可都眼巴巴盼着出来透气呢。
离完全找回手艺就差这么一小步了！加把劲，让我瞧瞧你当年的通天本领！
顺纹下刀，脆生利落；逆纹硬削，保准崩茬。木头的规矩就这么简单，全在你一念之间。
不用钉、不用胶，就这么硬碰硬咬在一块儿，千百年风雨都撼不动它分毫，这就是咱们的底气！
别慌，多试错几次算什么！哪位名匠在成为传奇之前，手底下没刨废过几方烂木头？
我在边上盯着呢，瞧你凿木头这认真的模样，倒真有当年几分大宗师的神气了！
lines_en: Yuan craftsmen were the boldest dreamers and doers of all! If the wood grew crooked, they carved the curve itself into a great beam—working with its nature, they called it!
Steady hands, open heart, bold strokes! Yuan mortises were cut broad and generous—none of that timid, hedging style. Commit to the cut!
If you can't tell where to join, open the Keen Eye and have a look. You're getting smoother with it all the time.
The wood grows on its own; people merely help it find its most comfortable place. Don't fight its grain—go along with it!
Well? Do you like how I look now? If you want a change of mood, pick me an outfit from the Wardrobe anytime—I'm at your call~
That last fit locked in solid! Hear that deep thud of wood biting wood? There's real backbone in that sound!
Back in the Yuan, builders dared to drop whole rows of thick columns from their great halls and let mortise-tenon beams carry the roof alone. Impressive, no?
Rotate it—try a few more angles. What looks seam-tight from the front may still hold room to give from the side.
Tired? These hefty members really do take it out of you. How about a two-minute rest? These centuries-old timbers aren't going anywhere.
Great skill looks clumsy; great straightness looks bent. Rough and homely as it appears, the tenons and mortises within are more precise than anyone's.
Saved up enough Talent yet? Then open a few more new outfits in the Wardrobe—several of my looks are longing to come out for a breath of air.
You're one small step from fully reclaiming your craft! Push on—show me that heaven-reaching skill of yours!
Cut with the grain: crisp and clean. Plane against it: you'll surely tear the fibers. The wood's rule is that simple—it all turns on your one thought.
No nails, no glue—wood gripping wood, hard against hard, unmoved by a thousand years of wind and rain. That is the ground we stand on!
Don't panic—what are a few failed tries? Before any famous master became a legend, how many boards had he planed to waste?
I'm watching from right here—and that earnest face of yours at the chisel already has a touch of the grand old master's air!
